sources.citation: Otronyi, Linus, John Muniru, Marcus Hansley, Carol Magnusson, Michael J. Rueck & Zachariah Yoder. 2011. Summary Report of a Sociolinguistic Survey of the Obanliku Speech Varieties of Cross River State, Nigeria. An Abridged Version of a Full Report. Jos: Language Development Facilitators, December 2011. 13 pp. (fetched sources from Wayback copy of the ResearchGate PDF)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (dialect inventory, 360-item wordlist similarity, RTT intelligibility, vitality, bilingualism in Bette). Only linguistic remark (p.2, sec. 2.2): Obanliku, Bette and Bendi 'share a similar basic word order (SVO), sound inventory and phonological and morphological compositions'. No mention of tone, stress, accent or syllable structure anywhere (full-text grep).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010 [2001]. The Bendi languages: more lost Bantu languages? Draft ms., Cambridge (32nd ACAL Benue-Congo workshop paper), 26 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative wordlists and classification of Bendi; Obanliku appears only in the population table (65,000; dialects Basang, Bebi, Bishiri, Bisu, Busi) and as wordlist columns. No prosody discussed.
No Scripture or literacy materials listed for Obanliku (only JESUS film dubs and GRN audio), i.e. no orthography statement surfaced through that channel.
